items.longBusinessSummary: Lumentum Holdings Inc. manufactures and sells optical and photonic products in the Americas, the Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. It offers component products, including semiconductor laser chips, laser sub-assemblies, line subsystems, and wavelength management systems. The company also offers system products, such as optical modules, optical circuit switches, and industrial lasers, including short-pulse solid-state lasers and kilowatt-class fiber lasers. Its products and solutions are used in cloud, artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML), telecommunications, consumer, and industrial end-market applications. The company was incorporated in 2015 and is headquartered in San Jose, California.

Lumentum Holdings has delivered extremely strong multi year share gains, which puts a spotlight on whether the current US$818.10 price is still aligned with the cash the business can generate. With the focus on its cash flows and a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) view available, the question is whether recent momentum has already pulled the valuation ahead of those fundamentals.
Over the past 3 years the stock has returned roughly 20 times an initial investment, which raises the stakes on whether the present valuation is still grounded in realistic cash flow assumptions.
The company's ability to translate its optical technology sales into reliable free cash flow, and how much reinvestment is needed to support that, can materially influence what its future stream of cash is worth today.

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model here is built around how much hard cash Lumentum Holdings can return to shareholders over time. Latest twelve month free cash flow sits at about $343.1 million, and the projections assume that this output does not stay flat. Analysts and model estimates point to rising annual free cash flows over the next decade that reach into the low single digit billions of dollars, before growth tapers to steadier levels.
That path matters because the valuation work suggests those future cash streams, when discounted back, imply an intrinsic worth that is substantially above the current $818.10 share price. Title: Lumentum stock surges 10% as AI components ‘completely sold out’
Author: Silin Chen   Mon, October 26, 2026 at 11:24 PM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-10-26T22:24:40+00:00
=== BODY ===
Lumentum Holdings (LITE) shares jumped about 8% to $818 on Monday, Oct. 26, after StoneX initiated coverage of the optical networking company with a Buy rating and a $1,200 price target.
The rally spread to other optical networking stocks. Coherent (COHR) and Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI) gained about 6% and 7%, respectively, while the Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF (LYTE) rose 4%.
StoneX said Lumentum occupies "critical scarcity points" in high-speed indium phosphide lasers, cloud transceivers and optical circuit switches, The Fly reported.
The analyst also highlighted management's comments that AI-related optoelectronic components were "completely sold out" through 2029, as Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston told Bloomberg earlier this month.
The new price target implies roughly 47% upside from Lumentum's afternoon trading price.
Lumentum, based in San Jose, California, makes lasers and optical components used in telecommunications networks and data centers.
The company has benefited largely from the AI infrastructure boom as tech hyperscalers spend billions of dollars building data centers that require faster connections between servers.
Related: Analysts revamp Super Micro stock price targets after 10% surge on revenue boost
One of its biggest backers is Nvidia (NVDA).
In March, Nvidia announced a multi-year strategic partnership with Lumentum to develop advanced optical technologies for next-generation AI infrastructure.
The agreement includes a multibillion-dollar purchase commitment from Nvidia and rights to access future manufacturing capacity for advanced laser components.
Nvidia also committed to invest $2 billion in Lumentum to support research and development and expand U.S. manufacturing, including a new fabrication facility.
"Together with Lumentum, NVIDIA is advancing the world's most sophisticated silicon photonics to build the next generation of gigawatt-scale AI factories," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in the announcement.
StoneX isn't the only firm optimistic about Lumentum.
On Oct. 20, Jefferies analyst Blayne Curtis raised his price target on Lumentum to $1,250 from $1,200 and maintained a Buy rating.
Curtis expects Lumentum to capture a larger share of Alphabet's (GOOGL) optical circuit switching demand and benefit from growing adoption of 1.6T transceivers.
Jefferies also expects Lumentum to become Alphabet's largest optical circuit switch supplier next year, overtaking the tech giant's in-house production.
Lumentum's latest quarterly results showed strong demand for its optical networking products.
In its fiscal fourth quarter ended June 27, the company reported revenue of $1.01 billion, up 109.3% from $480.7 million a year earlier. Adjusted earnings rose to $3.23 per share from $0.88 a year earlier.
For fiscal 2026, revenue reached $3.01 billion, compared with $1.6 billion in fiscal 2025.
Also read: Meta stock falls despite Wall Street analysts raising price targets
The company expects fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenue of $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion, with adjusted earnings of $4.05 to $4.35 per share.
Lumentum is scheduled to report its next quarterly results on Nov. 5.
Investors will be watching closely whether the company can expand production quickly enough to meet demand, as well as its outlook for cloud networking revenue and profit margins.
Lumentum shares have gained 122% so far in 2026, as of this writing, although the stock has pulled back sharply from its recent all-time high of $1,143, reached on October 8.
Related: Cathie Wood buys $24.5 million of tumbling megacap stock

Title: Stock Market Today, Oct. 26: AI Optimism Lifts Nasdaq as Tech Stocks Rebound
Author: Robert Izquierdo, The Motley Fool   Mon, October 26, 2026 at 10:50 PM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-10-26T21:50:00+00:00
=== BODY ===
The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) gained 0.70% to 7,677, the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) rose 0.82% to 26,169 as AI optimism returned, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI) edged up 0.28% to 52,362, diverging from Friday's energy-driven session as oil prices retreated.
Gold prices rose 0.46% to $4,026.30 as of U.S. market close and the 10-Year Treasury yield rose 0.04% to 5%, with investors favoring Real Estate and Technology stocks while Communication Services shares faced selling pressure.
Surgery Partners (NASDAQ:SGRY) soared 48% on reports of a majority-stake takeover negotiation, while Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) jumped 8% following a bullish price target initiation. Conversely, Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) fell 2% after filing to raise capital for AI infrastructure, and Petrobras (NYSE:PBR) plunged 14% following election results in Brazil.
The big driver for Wall Street's tech stock rally on Oct. 26, 2026 was the long-awaited initial public offering (IPO) filing by artificial intelligence giant Anthropic. The company filed its S-1 prospectus to go public on the Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT." Its massive revenue growth figures in the filing calmed investor fears that the artificial intelligence boom was losing steam.
Anthropic's IPO revived enthusiasm for technology stocks, helping the Nasdaq Composite lead the market today despite pressure on more mature communication services providers. Adding to today's market performance was Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) stock gaining over 5%. Barclays upgraded shares to an Overweight rating, and raised its price target from $370 to $450 due to potential ties with CEO Elon Musk's other company, SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX), growth in Tesla's robotaxi business, and a recovery in its core automotive operations.
Meanwhile, Meta Platforms shares slipped after the company disclosed plans to raise up to $95 billion for AI infrastructure, signaling that the immense capital requirements for industry dominance remain a primary concern for mega-cap investors. Next, investors are looking ahead to this week's earnings from Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) and the upcoming Federal Reserve interest rate decision, which will determine if the current momentum can survive tightening financial conditions.
